sources.title: Introducing Devin
sources.finding: Devin cloud provides shell, IDE and interactive browser tools; local CLI can hand work to cloud.

sources.title: Devin pricing
sources.finding: Free desktop access differs from Pro cloud access; Teams has a base fee plus full developer seats, while quota amounts are not fixed in the FAQ.

sources.title: Devin API overview
sources.finding: The v3 organization and enterprise APIs manage sessions and context resources with service users or personal tokens; attribution requires defined permissions.

sources.title: Security profiles
sources.finding: Security profiles separately restrict network, external MCP, Devin-management tools and Git writes; child sessions inherit the profile chain.

sources.title: Welcome to Devin Desktop
sources.finding: Devin Desktop installs on macOS, Windows and Linux; its primary local harness is Devin Local, shared with Devin CLI. A Devin account is required; cloud and local workflows remain distinct.

sources.title: Devin CLI Quickstart
sources.finding: Devin CLI runs locally on macOS, Linux and Windows. Cloud Devin runs in a VM. CLI currently does not support account Knowledge, Playbooks or Secrets; these are planned, not shipped.

sources.title: Devin Cloud in the Devin CLI
sources.locator: Start; Resume; Continue locally; Local Hands
sources.finding: Cloud sessions run on their own VM and continue when the terminal closes. Resume accepts a session URL/ID. Pickup checks out the PR branch locally; Local Hands requires per-call approval.

sources.title: Devin CLI Subagents
sources.locator: How Subagents Work; Cost; Model profiles
sources.finding: Foreground children wait with interactive approvals; background children run concurrently and deny unapproved tools. The parent receives completion and summarizes results. Each child has independent inference costs and profile-selected model.

sources.title: Devin Knowledge
sources.finding: Knowledge stores shared instructions, supports trigger retrieval and repo/organization/enterprise scope, user toggles and corrections. It is deprecated and gradually migrating to Skills in Plugins; future removal has no stated date.

sources.title: Session Insights
sources.finding: Completed sessions have free Insights with usage, message count, size classification, issue timeline and knowledge analysis. Full large-session analysis is automatic; smaller sessions can request analysis through UI or API.

sources.title: Devin Review
sources.locator: Features; Reading a Review; PR Workflow Actions; Permissions
sources.finding: Devin Review displays grouped diffs, supports comments and request changes, retains analyses and CI status, and offers provider-dependent PR workflow actions. Write actions require appropriate connected identities and permissions.

sources.title: Security at Cognition
sources.locator: Privacy and IP; Retention; Third-party audits
sources.finding: Cognition states SOC 2 Type II since September 2024. Training is on by default except Enterprise without written consent; paid users can opt out. Customer data is retained during the relationship, while interaction/feedback retention is separately determined.

sources.title: Devin Plans and Pricing
sources.finding: Free desktop access has a light agent quota. Pro costs $20/month, Max $200. Teams charge $80/month plus $40/full-development seat. Paid usage allowances refresh daily and weekly; extra usage is at API pricing.

sources.title: Welcome to Devin Desktop
sources.locator: Set Up > Linux deb/rpm repository notes; Uninstall > Windows pre-rename folder note
sources.finding: Vendor explicitly calls windsurf repository names pre-rebrand, names devin-desktop as the new package, and retains a transitional windsurf package for existing installs. Windows installations from before the rename may retain a Windsurf folder. This establishes the editor lineage, not a former name for Devin cloud.

sources.title: Devin Desktop Agent Client Protocol
sources.finding: Desktop explicitly supports Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenCode and Gemini CLI through ACP. It also supports custom ACP agents; the list is examples, not exhaustive. Agent binaries must already be installed. External agents handle their own /login and provider billing. Free/Pro/Max/Teams support ACP; Enterprise third-party agents need enablement.

sources.title: Devin Outposts
sources.finding: Outposts runs command execution, file edits and repository access on user machines, VMs, containers or Kubernetes. The agent loop, inference and planning remain in Devin Cloud. Workers claim sessions from a named queue; N workers serve N concurrent sessions.

sources.title: Devin Local
sources.finding: Devin Local is the Devin CLI harness inside Desktop; it can run a session in a Git worktree and merge changes back into the workspace.

sources.title: Devin Desktop advanced configuration
sources.finding: Desktop can open/reopen a workspace in a devcontainer.json-defined container or attach to a running Docker container, including from SSH windows.

sources.title: Devin current plans and pricing
sources.finding: Free is $0; Pro is $20/month; Max $200/month; Teams is $80/month plus $40/month per full development seat; Enterprise is contact sales. Pro, Max and Teams explicitly list Use your ChatGPT plan. Teams explicitly lists multiplayer sessions. Paid overages are at API pricing; there is no separate compute or one-time plan in the complete list.

sources.title: Devin Slack collaboration
sources.locator: Sync sessions with Slack threads; Code channels
sources.finding: Sessions sync bidirectionally with Slack threads: web messages appear in the thread and thread replies reach Devin. A code channel is dedicated to one session and every message sent in it goes to that session; documentation describes team collaboration on runs.

sources.title: Cognition terms of service
sources.finding: Sections 2.1 and 3.1 reserve Cognition rights in the Services and grant a non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-sublicensable right to use the Services for internal business purposes. These are proprietary service terms, separate from user ownership of outputs.

sources.title: Devin Desktop
sources.locator: Hero product UI; Coordinate your agent swarm; Handoff between local and cloud; Instant codebase context; Built-in Devin Review; integrations list
sources.finding: Product page depicts the Agent Command Center board with Status/Space/Pull request/Agent filters, Running/Waiting for review/Done columns and session states (Working, PR is ready, Waiting for CI, No PR, Merged, Closed, PR is approved); a coordinator session splitting work into subagents that each open PRs; local-to-cloud handoff keeping the same conversation and branch; Fast Context; built-in Devin Review findings; integrations including Linear (create and update issues and projects) and Atlassian (Jira and Confluence). Research-preview multi-agent support is mentioned in a customer quote. UI content is vendor illustration.

sources.title: Devin CLI
sources.locator: Feature sections; Everything in the box command and control lists
sources.finding: Devin CLI is described as built in Rust; MCP servers, skills, hooks and Claude Code plugins work as-is; AGENTS.md loads automatically. Commands: /model (model, effort, Fusion), /handoff to Devin Cloud, /loop implement then auto-review, /plan, /ask, /fork, /revert (roll files and conversation back to a step), /resume, /share (send the session to your team), devin -p single-turn mode for scripts and CI. Controls: Normal, Accept Edits, Smart, Bypass, Autonomous (OS sandbox), --sandbox fail-closed isolation, subagents (foreground/background), custom subagents, allow/ask/deny rules per tool and path, admin-enforced team settings, hooks, image paste.

sources.title: Plans and Pricing
sources.finding: Free $0 (light quota, limited model availability, unlimited Tab and inline edits); Pro $20/month (increased quotas, full model availability, Devin Cloud, extra usage at API pricing); Max $200/month; Teams $80/month (up to 100 users, multiplayer sessions, 2 concurrent Free-mode sessions per user, SAML/OIDC SSO, 3 usage tiers, Slack channel support); Enterprise contact sales (highest priority support, dedicated account management, SCIM and RBAC, dedicated deployment, VPC). Comparison lists concurrent sessions limit Up to 10, Up to 10, Unlimited, Unlimited across the plan columns; integrations GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and custom git providers. Paid plans have daily/weekly refreshing allowances; extra usage is bought at API pricing.

sources.title: Self-serve plans
sources.locator: Plan overview; Free; Pro; Max; Teams; How quotas work; On-demand credits
sources.finding: Teams is a flat $80/month charged as prepaid on-demand credits shared by all members (no per-seat price); Pro and Max are single-user. Pro has daily and weekly allowances, Max weekly only; Teams has no per-member allowance. Past the allowance, prepaid on-demand credits (roll over) fund usage; sessions pause when credits run out. Teams members can run up to 2 Free (SWE-2) cloud sessions at a time; Jira and Microsoft Teams integrations are Enterprise only. Quota sizes are not stated.

sources.title: Devin Enterprise
sources.locator: Model Wisdom; Outcomes Win; No Shadows; AI Analytics; AI Cost Controls; Security & Trust; FAQ
sources.finding: Admins can restrict models on Desktop and CLI and modes on Cloud. An ACU is the normalized measure of a task, model and machine included; budgets, caps and the guarantee count in ACUs. Usage tiers with monthly ACU allocations per organization, tier and person hold until an admin changes them; members request more inside Devin and admins approve or deny. Analytics show value against spend by team, repository and project on a record that cannot be edited after the fact; billing tags. Every session runs on its own machine with kernel-level isolation, secrets stay out of the prompt, IP access lists; single-tenant and your region if needed; audit log with exports and API; self-hosted SCM (GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab self-managed, Azure DevOps Server, Bitbucket Data Center, Gerrit, Perforce).

sources.title: Devin Security
sources.finding: Lists comprehensive audit logs, kernel-level session isolation, private networking, multiple deployment options and custom deployment regions, and custom retention policies.

sources.title: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop
sources.locator: Agent Command Center; Devin Desktop is not just for Devin; The power of an IDE; Introducing Devin Local
sources.finding: Devin Desktop builds on the Windsurf IDE; the Agent Command Center Kanban view manages local and cloud agents, and Spaces group sessions, PRs, files and context. ACP agents (Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode, in-house agents) appear in the Kanban view and Spaces like Devin sessions. The IDE stays backwards-compatible with Windsurf and VS Code extensions. Devin Local, the successor to Cascade, was rewritten in Rust and supports subagents.

sources.title: Download Devin Desktop
sources.finding: Devin Desktop downloads for macOS, Windows and Linux; Devin Next (Beta) for early adopters; Windsurf JetBrains plugin still offered; upgrading from Windsurf carries over plan, pricing, extensions, settings and in-progress work.

sources.title: Devin Docs: English API index
sources.locator: Sessions; Devin Review; Knowledge Notes; Playbooks; Secrets; Repositories; Snapshot Setup; Automations; Schedules; Git Permissions; Analytics; Consumption; Audit Logs; Queue; Hypervisors; Users; Service Users; Tags; IP Access List; Organization Settings
sources.finding: The v3 API reference lists sessions (create, list messages chronologically, send a message that resumes the session, list attachments, terminate, archive and put to sleep, tags), Devin Review trigger/status, knowledge notes and playbooks CRUD, org secrets, repository indexing and status, blueprints and snapshot builds (manual trigger, cancel, logs, pin builds under 7 days old), automations with trigger event schemas and templates, schedules, git permissions, metrics (usage, sessions by category, PRs, searches), daily ACU consumption by enterprise/org/user/service user/session, audit logs, enterprise queue status, customer-VPC hypervisors, user invite/update/delete, service-user API key revoke/rotate, allowed session tags, IP access lists and organization default session platform; v1/v2 are legacy with a migration guide and several sections are marked Beta.

sources.locator: CLI Getting Started, Editor Integrations, Extensibility, Enterprise and Federal sections
sources.finding: Index describes CLI pages for subagents (foreground/background), cloud sessions (create, steer, resume, watch), SSH and devin forward, handoff, models (Adaptive routing, Fusion), sandbox (OS-level isolation, network filtering, enterprise enforcement); ACP integrations for JetBrains, Zed and Xcode; extensibility via rules/AGENTS.md, skills (SKILL.md with own permissions), plugins and team marketplace, MCP (add, configure, authenticate), hooks and configuration import; enterprise environment rollout health, Devin Connect, local agent controls, usage policies, SSO/SCIM/IdP groups; Federal Python SDK.

sources.title: Agent Command Center
sources.finding: The Agent Command Center manages local and cloud agents in one view; the sidebar filters, sorts and groups sessions and can start child sessions; one native OS notification per session when an agent finishes or needs input (off by default, devin.agentNotifications).

sources.title: Agent Client Protocol
sources.locator: Overview notes; Example agents; Enabling custom agents
sources.finding: Third-party ACP agents (Codex CLI, Claude Agent, OpenCode, Junie, Gemini CLI, custom) run in the Agent Command Center beside Devin Local on Free, Pro, Max and Teams; off by default on Enterprise. External agents bill directly with their provider.

sources.title: Hand off to cloud Devins
sources.locator: Overview; What carries over; Hand off back to local
sources.finding: /handoff moves the CLI session to a cloud Devin VM with repo, branch, conversation context and uncommitted changes, so work continues after the laptop closes; progress is tracked from the terminal or web app; /handoff in a cloud session fetches its PR branch and continues locally.

sources.title: Sandbox
sources.locator: How the sandbox works; Network filtering; Excluded commands
sources.finding: --sandbox enforces writable paths and Read deny rules at the OS level and refuses to start if sandboxing is unavailable (fail-closed); not supported on Windows; Linux needs bubblewrap and socat. Domain allow/deny network filtering through a loopback proxy is marked currently unstable.

sources.title: Devin CLI permissions
sources.locator: Default Permission Behavior; Smart Mode; Autonomous Mode; How Permissions Work
sources.finding: Normal (default) auto-approves reads and prompts for writes, fetches and shell; approvals can be once, session, project or always. Accept Edits, Smart (model-judged, never auto-approves installs, rm/sudo, mutating git), Bypass and Autonomous (only with the OS sandbox) modes exist. Deny rules win over ask and allow; organization deny/ask rules from Team Settings stay active in every mode.

sources.title: Subagents
sources.finding: The main agent spawns subagents with selectable profiles in the foreground (user approves tools) or background (parent notified on completion). Subagents cannot spawn subagents by default; custom profiles can opt in with max-nesting.

sources.title: Models
sources.finding: Devin CLI supports models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Cognition plus open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM; Fusion and Adaptive routing; /model switches models during a session.

sources.title: Commands & Flags
sources.finding: /fork [step], /revert [step] (revert file changes from a step and rewind the conversation), /resume, /continue, /recap, /export; essential commands add devin -p single-turn mode, Esc Esc to cancel the running agent, image paste and devin --cloud to create/resume cloud sessions.

sources.title: Configuration Import
sources.finding: Devin CLI imports rules and configuration found in the project from Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Kiro, OpenCode and Zed.

sources.title: Usage
sources.finding: Idle sessions go to sleep and consume no usage; Devin sleeps after 5 minutes of inactivity by default (30 minutes for some Windows or GPU machines), and a new message wakes the session.

sources.title: Usage policies: budgets and user limits
sources.locator: Overview; Additional usage requests; Approval policies
sources.finding: Enterprise budgets and per-member limits (tiers, IdP group mappings, overrides) cap ACU usage; local and cloud usage count against the same limits and new work is blocked on all surfaces at a limit; members request more and approval policies decide.

sources.title: Secrets & Site Cookies
sources.locator: Giving Devin Credentials; personal and repository secrets
sources.finding: Organization, personal, repository and session secrets; Redact value is on by default and a redacted value cannot be shown again; repository secrets are stored encrypted and never written into blueprints or snapshots.

sources.title: Devin Connect
sources.finding: A customer-run gateway is an HTTP CONNECT policy proxy with a default-deny allowlist enforced on both the gateway and Devin side, reached over an outbound-only tunnel or AWS PrivateLink.

sources.title: Devin Outposts: self-hosted infrastructure
sources.finding: Outposts run session command execution, file edits and repository access on customer VMs, containers, Kubernetes or Macs, while the agent loop stays in Devin cloud.

sources.title: Devin environment setup
sources.finding: Environment setup configures repos, tools, dependencies, environment variables and secrets so sessions start ready, using org- and repo-tier blueprints built into snapshots.

sources.title: Fast Context
sources.finding: Fast Context is a subagent in Devin Desktop that retrieves relevant code up to 20x faster using SWE-grep models.

sources.title: Devin browser previews
sources.finding: A browser preview is a private link to a web app running on Devin's machine; Devin exposes the port of a dev server it starts.

sources.title: Scheduled Sessions
sources.finding: Legacy scheduled sessions are managed here; new recurring or one-time scheduled work is created as automations with a Schedule trigger.

sources.title: Index a Repository
sources.finding: Repositories are indexed from DeepWiki settings to power Ask Devin and DeepWiki.
